newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean bourse launches new trading system Monday.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean bourse launches new trading system Monday.

text.p: The Korea Stock Exchange will launch a new electronic trading system on Monday, November 25, the exchange said on Friday.

The exchange said in a statement that its computer system will be upgraded to handle up to one million orders a day from the previous 650,000 orders. The new system will also be able to accommodate as many as 2,100 listed issues.
Along with the new system, the exchange will introduce an after-hours trading session and two new forms of market orders on Monday, the statement said.
The exchange will adopt the after-hours session "to provide investors with additional opportunities to buy and sell shares after the close of the trading hour," the statement said.
The session will be held for 30 minutes after normal trading ends, and orders will be executed at the closing price of each listed stock.
Investors will be able to place market orders and limit-or-market-on-close orders, in addition to the present limit orders, it said.
A market order is an order to buy or sell a stock at the best available price.

A limit order is an order to buy or sell a stock at a specific price or better, while a limit-or-market-on-close order is an order that becomes a market order if it is not executed during trading hours.
Block-trades will also be possible during the after-hours session. To be eligible, the block order should be for more than 50,000 shares or worth more than one billion won, the exchange said.
